:::{#def-intersection}
#### Intersection

The **intersection** of sets $A$ and $B$,
written $A \cap B$,
is the set of elements that are in both $A$ and $B$:

$$A \cap B \eqdef \set{x : x \in A \text{ and } x \in B}$$

More generally, let $I$ be a nonempty set of indices,
such as $\cb{1, \ldots, n}$ or $\cb{1, 2, 3, \ldots}$,
and let $A_i$ be a set for each $i \in I$.
The intersection of the sets $A_i$,
written $\bigcap_{i \in I} A_i$,
is the set of elements that are in every $A_i$.
For $I = \cb{1, \ldots, n}$, it is also written $\bigcap_{i=1}^{n} A_i$ or $A_1 \cap \cdots \cap A_n$,
and for $I = \cb{1, 2, 3, \ldots}$, it is written $\bigcap_{i=1}^{\infty} A_i$.

:::
